solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Lady Muck initially rich as one's poor

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word Muck
poor suggests something in bad shape, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark that a self-important woman is only rich because someone else is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' is the anagram signal, and the S of one's counts as a letter. 'Lady Muck' is British slang for a woman who gives herself airs, so 'Muck' looks like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness is a noblewoman, wife of a marquess, and so properly addressed as Lady.

clue.text: Very distant rising endlessly going on

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from the bottom upward
endlessly says the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: too far is a way of saying very distant

explanation.surface: Something very far off is gradually coming up into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TOO FAR to TOOFA, and 'rising' turns that over to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoot means in progress or happening, a synonym of going on.

clue.text: Fall for rogue in suit

indicators.note: in places the rogue's letters inside the word for suit

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue

explanation.surface: A scoundrel in a smart suit taking the blame for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a legal case here, not clothing; 'Fall' is a noun, a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a small waterfall, so a fall of water.

clue.text: De Niro nicely demonstrates sneering

indicators.note: demonstrates means the run of letters is shown openly within De Niro nicely

explanation.surface: An actor showing off a mocking expression in a film performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic and sneering both describe mocking, sardonic speech or manner.

clue.text: Lord Muck initially in list supporting aristocrat

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts one piece beneath the other

parts.note: a nob is informal British slang for an upper-class person

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for list

parts.note: a ship lists when it leans to one side

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of Muck

explanation.surface: A pompous peer whose name appears on a list of the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord Muck' is British slang for a self-important man, but only Lord defines; 'list' is the verb a tilting ship does, and 'supporting' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman holds a peerage and may be styled Lord.

clue.text: Professional done in by end of aerobics

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of the word aerobics

parts.note: done in is slang for killed

explanation.surface: A fitness instructor exhausted at the end of an aerobics class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done in' reads as worn out but means murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Professional and skilled both describe someone expert and competent at a trade.

clue.text: Plug a test drive with men behaving badly

indicators.note: behaving badly suggests misconduct, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A car commercial featuring a test drive by unruly lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men Behaving Badly' was a British sitcom about laddish flatmates, which dresses the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is an informal word for a promotion or advertising mention.

clue.text: Handled pipe to cut supply

parts.note: describes a valve in a water pipe turned by a handle to shut off the flow, while hinting at smoking a pipe

explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is a valve with a handle fitted to a pipe for shutting off water.

clue.text: Turning mean, tried it on, showing tenacity

indicators.note: turning suggests a change of course, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone becoming nasty after trying it on, yet showing persistence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tried it on' is British slang for attempting a cheeky deception.
explanation.definitionFit: Determination is a synonym of tenacity: firm persistence of purpose.

clue.text: Doctor's including operation for eye treatment

indicators.note: including means the doctors' abbreviation holds the operation inside it

parts.note: Dr's, read as DRS, the plural abbreviation of doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's practice offering surgery as an eye treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye drops are a common liquid treatment applied to the eyes.

clue.text: Be let out I fancy from dungeon

indicators.note: fancy suggests something elaborate or imaginative, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A prisoner begging to be released from a dungeon.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon reached only through a trapdoor above.

clue.text: Kick out former wife with occupation about sex

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: about means the occupation word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a trade is an occupation or line of work
it is a coy slang word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Throwing out an ex-wife whose job involves selling sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as a word for sex is old slang, as in a film star said to have 'it'; 'about' wraps the occupation round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To extradite is to send someone out of a country to face trial elsewhere, a formal kicking out.

clue.text: Liberal section of church backsliding

parts.note: an apse is a domed recess at the end of a church

explanation.surface: A liberal faction of a church drifting away from its principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' looks like a reversal signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a falling back from standards, which is backsliding in noun form.

clue.text: Stagger one regularly getting into scrap?

definitions.meaning: a rag-and-bone collector who habitually picks up scrap, playing on a fight-prone person

explanation.definitionFit: Stagger is a synonym for walking unsteadily; in British slang the same word names a scrap collector.

clue.text: 'Time', track's gripping Queen previews

indicators.note: gripping means the track word holds the queen inside it

parts.note: track's read as rail's, rails being a track
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: Announcing the time while a track features a Queen song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the rock band but gives the royal cipher; 'track's' supplies its S as a letter, as if rail's.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailers are short previews advertising a coming film.

clue.text: Anchor tug overturned creating mess for crew

indicators.note: overturned turns the whole joined run of letters back to front

parts.note: to moor a boat is to anchor it
to draw is to pull or tug

explanation.surface: A capsized tugboat causing chaos for its sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardroom is the officers' mess on a warship, so a mess for part of the crew.

clue.text: Tailless rodent, small, also called foreign delicacy

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent
aka stands for also known as

explanation.surface: A little mouse without a tail renamed as an exotic dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a Greek baked dish of aubergine and meat, a foreign delicacy to a British solver.

clue.text: Arches back before steamy photo

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second
back means the word for arches is read in reverse

parts.note: spans are arches of a bridge
steamy means hot

explanation.surface: A racy photograph with someone arching their back.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly.

clue.text: Ray, a French bachelor in bed

indicators.note: in puts the two pieces inside the word for bed

parts.note: a seam is a bed or layer of coal or rock
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A Frenchman named Ray, a bachelor, lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a ray of sunlight.

clue.text: Verbal nudge in case of solicitation

indicators.note: in places the nudge word inside the outer letters
case of means the outer letters of solicitation, its shell

parts.note: a poke is a nudge

explanation.surface: A gentle nudge given in the course of soliciting.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbal and spoken both mean expressed in words, said aloud rather than written.

clue.text: Dives and dives under surface of pool

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts the second piece beneath the first
surface of asks for the top letter of the word pool

parts.note: lunges are dives forward

explanation.surface: A swimmer diving and diving again beneath the water's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to dive headlong, so plunges means dives.

clue.text: He wants the lot!

parts.note: reads as a greedy person, but describes someone at an auction seeking a lot under the hammer

explanation.definitionFit: At an auction a bidder offers money to secure a particular lot.

clue.text: Cove encircles the Italian city

indicators.note: encircles means the word for cove surrounds the other piece

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A bay surrounding an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cove' looks like a bay but is old slang for a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is a major city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Viagra perhaps, man with lust it excited

indicators.note: excited suggests agitation, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A lustful man taking Viagra and getting aroused.
explanation.definitionFit: Viagra is an example of a stimulant drug; perhaps signals the example.

clue.text: Drink one's consumed inside part of church

indicators.note: consumed inside means the drink word swallows the other piece

parts.note: ale is a drink
one's read as I'S, I being one

explanation.surface: Someone drinking secretly during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage or side section running through a church.

clue.text: Nanny state's first in ruin, made to change

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the rearranged letters
to change means the letters of the words are rearranged
first takes only the opening letter of state's

explanation.surface: A complaint that the nanny state is wrecking things and forcing change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' turns RUINMADE into NUREMAID, and S goes in after NUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after children, a nanny.

clue.text: Touch of wind over relish

parts.note: a gust is a brief touch of wind
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A breeze blowing over a jar of relish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means enjoyment or zest, a synonym of relish.

clue.text: Red setter returned, secured around rear

indicators.note: returned means the word for the setter is read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: around means the secured word goes about the other piece

parts.note: barred means secured, as a door is
ass is slang for the rear or bottom

explanation.surface: A red setter dog brought back and tied up by its hindquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red setter' reads as the dog breed but the colour is the definition; ASS goes into BARRED as BARR-ASS-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed goes red in the face, so red means blushing with shame.
